x: With half-a mile to go Anderson, the Police Champion, and Rangit moved away from Mal after the three had interchanged the lead all the way. When 300 yards out Mal began to sprint and had caught and had his nose in front by the home straight.

Great running came from Neil Owen whose 13.60, behind the American Anderson's 13.38, removed John Ridgeon's 13.62 from our record books. Neil was also significantly faster than his rival for a World Champs. team place, Andy Tulloch, who ran in the 'A' race.
But no, it wasn’t Miles, Anderson & Co. venting their frustration at being pipped by Salford Harriers – it was the world famous Horwich RMI Clog Dancers.
